You have watched an app take over your feed and assumed it was luck, one video that happened to pop. The truth is far more boring and far more brutal, and almost nobody who has actually done it will say it out loud. I spent two years building the influencer machine behind Cal AI, taking it from about 20 creators to more than 200 posting at once while the app peaked at 60 million dollars a year, and here I pull back the curtain on exactly how it ran.

I show you the golden moment we built every deal around, why our best converting videos barely mentioned the app, and the 15 second rule behind every post. I break down the minimum view clause that let creators set our own floor, the CPM math that made us more profitable as the niche saturated, the niches that printed, and why recipe and mukbang content never converted. Then I cover the outreach machine, 25 assistants sending 2,000 emails a day, 220,000 creators contacted to sign roughly 2,000 of them, the referral bonuses that got us past agents, and where I would put my money now.
